Inspection for Flat 12, 162 Beacon Close, Cedarford, ZZ9 5ZZ. Appointment date: 16 February 2024. Assessor: assessor named in the report. Agency: Northbridge Lettings.

The report provides an impartial, room-by-room schedule of condition for the main property features and any contents. Where the assessor makes no comment on an element or item, it is taken to be in good, clean, serviceable condition and without defects. Defects or elements in poor condition observed during inspection are to be identified in the narrative and evidenced with photographs.

Descriptions such as 'silver', 'chrome' and 'oak' refer to appearance and not necessarily the actual material. Listed items are described for identification. Items are described as new only when in a new or newly refurbished building, or still in manufacturer wrapping. In a property that is not new or newly refurbished, some wear and tear is assumed unless otherwise noted.

The report preparer is not an expert on fabrics, woods, materials, antiques or similar items. The report will not necessarily mention structural defects and does not advise on repairs or their cost. Fixtures and fittings are listed and described, but may not have been tested.

The assessor visually inspects the interior of the main building and contents, and generally inspects the remainder of the building, including exterior cosmetic elements and permanent outbuildings. Inaccessible areas and loft areas are not inspected. Belongings left by the landlord in a locked room or outbuildings are not inspected and remain the landlord's responsibility. Items of little monetary value are listed and described generically.

The report remains the property of the instructing party and shall not be used without written permission.

At the end of the tenancy, the property and its contents are expected to be in a similar condition and state of cleanliness to that recorded before the tenancy began. Damage believed to exceed fair wear and tear may need repair or replacement, with the cost deducted from the tenant's deposit. Receipts should be retained and produced if required.

If cleaning is unsatisfactory, a managing agent or landlord may instruct a professional cleaner; the cost if this will be deducted from the tenant's deposit. Receipts should be retained where professional cleaners are used. Cleaning must be thorough and the property left tidy at the end of the tenancy.

Carpets should be professionally cleaned before the end of the tenancy in accordance with the inventory or tenancy agreement. Vinyl or tile flooring should be clean and free from cracks or tears. Curtains should be professionally cleaned in accordance with the inventory or tenancy agreement.

The decor should remain in the same state and condition as at the start of the tenancy. Charges may be incurred if picture hooks, nails, screws or screw holes are added and not removed or repaired satisfactorily. Excessive marks and fingerprints should be removed; fingerprints on walls and doors are considered a cleaning issue, although reasonable wear and tear is expected.
